claude.rationale: The slice documents a whole-company cash-out reverse-triangular merger in which DST's entire legal entity, "all reported segments," products, and operations crossed together with "no operating business, product line, or segment of DST... carved out or excluded," so product (T4) and its producing processes (T5) moved as a unit — gap_45 = 0. The management/organization also crossed with the entity (retention plan to "preserve intact its present business organization" and equity-conversion for continuing officers), so processes and the people/organization running them transferred together — gap_56 = 0. Because the entire going concern moved as one whole-company acquisition with no carve-out, there is no structural product/process or process/organization mismatch at closing; the CEO/one executive departures via negotiated severance do not sever the operating organization from its processes at the structural tier.

grok.rationale: The slice states the whole legal entity crossed as a going concern via reverse-triangular merger with no operating business, product line, or segment carved out, so T4 product and T5 processes moved together (gap_45=0). Pre-closing covenants required DST to preserve intact its present business organization, a retention plan aimed at management continuity, and no TSA was used because nothing was left behind, so T5 and T6 aligned at closing (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: DST and all its subsidiaries crossed as a going concern, with no operating business, product line, or segment carved out, so the customer-facing offerings and their operating processes transferred together [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-011059, DEFM14A]. DST was required to preserve its business organization through closing, and its management structure crossed subject to documented retention, severance, and equity-conversion arrangements; therefore, no closing-structure process-versus-organization gap is documented [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-011059, DEFM14A, merger agreement Section 5.01].
